title: Identity past BasicCredential becomes an exploitable asymmetry, not a documented weakness
description:
Mark, 2026-11-22, hard blocker.

AGENTS.md lists this as a deliberate weakness: "BasicCredential by
default, so a provider can claim any identity for its own users unless
they use the did:webvh credential (mimid-1wgh.4.81)."

Mark's point is that the weakness changes character under a mandate.
Today it is a documented limitation among cooperating implementations.
With competitors FORCED to carry each other's traffic, a provider that
can mint any identity for its own users holds an exploitable asymmetry
against a competitor obliged to accept it. The incentive to abuse it
exists precisely because the parties are not friendly.

The remedy exists: mls-didwebvh (draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential,
epic mimid-1wgh.4.81), which mimid implements. The problem is that a
credential only helps if the OTHER side checks it, so this needs the WG
to settle identity, not just mimid to ship it. Same shape as catch-up:
the specification work matters more than the implementation.

Related open work: mimid-1wgh.4.81.38 (read and show the did:key entries
of a verified did:webvh log), and the IANA code points are still
unassigned (mimid-1wgh.4.81.18), which is itself a sign of how unsettled
this is.

Nothing to build here beyond what .4.81 already tracks. The bead exists
to record WHY its priority changes if interop is mandated, so it is not
left as "a deliberate weakness" in a world where that is no longer a
safe thing to be.
